name: cry_pidgey
note: the shortest cry sample (1902 samples, 0.18 s): the cry player's chain position, the template's start tick, the channel dying long before the 140-tick EOT

name: cry_bulbasaur
note: gCryTable[0], a typical length (8183 samples, 0.78 s)

name: cry_wailord
note: a long cry (20846 samples, 1.98 s); 3 s covers the sample end and the EOT / FINE tick at 140

name: cry_jynx
note: the longest cry sample (23524 samples, 2.24 s), still over before the 140-tick EOT; no cry sample loops

name: cry_jynx_faint
note: Cry_Jynx at CRY_MODE_FAINT's pitch 14440 (TIE key 56, TUNE 116): the sample would run 2.75 s, so it is still sounding at the 140-tick EOT -- the first cry whose ply_endtie finds a chained channel holding the key (the measured +28) and whose release-0 cut is audible; ply_fine then unlinks the live channel

name: cry_bulbasaur_howl
note: Cry_Bulbasaur at CRY_MODE_HIGH_PITCH's pitch 15800 (TIE key 62, TUNE 28; Howl's pitch without its chorus / length / release) panned hard right (pan 63 as the game's opponent side, PAN byte 0x7F): a non-zero pan through ChnVolSetAsm

name: cry_pidgey_quiet
note: Cry_Pidgey at volume 90 (CRY_MODE_ENCOUNTER / HIGH_PITCH's value, VOL byte 0x5A) at the default pitch and pan

name: cry_jynx_faint_full
note: Cry_Jynx with CRY_MODE_FAINT complete (pitch 14440, length 140, release 200; the mode sets no chorus): the twin of cry_jynx_faint whose EOT releases the still-sounding channel instead of cutting it -- the first release tail on a DPCM channel in the corpus (envelope 255 * 200 >> 8 per frame from the EOT on frame 143, the channel stopped on frame 161 when the product reaches 0); ply_fine unlinks the releasing channel

name: cry_wailord_doubles
note: Cry_Wailord with CRY_MODE_DOUBLES (length 20, release 225, pitch 15360; the mode sets no chorus): the 1.98 s sample cut by the EOT at tick 20 (frame 23) with the slowest release, 30 release frames to the channel's stop on frame 53

name: cry_pidgey_roar2
note: Cry_Pidgey with CRY_MODE_ROAR_2 (length 60, release 225, pitch 15616 = TIE key 61; the mode sets no chorus): the 0.17 s sample has ended long before tick 60 (the unlink tick on frame 14), so the EOT on frame 63 finds an empty chain and only the xWAIT length changes against cry_pidgey; the xRELE byte reaches no channel

name: cry_bulbasaur_reverse
note: gCryTable_Reverse[0] = gCryTable[388] (cry_reverse Cry_Bulbasaur, ToneData type 0x30 = CMP | REV, the same 8183-sample DPCM data as cry_bulbasaur) at CRY_MODE_NORMAL's defaults: SoundMainRAM_Unk1's reversed DPCM walk in isolation, the sample played from its last block to its first and running out through the count path (the unlink tick on frame 50)

name: cry_jynx_growl1
note: cry_reverse Cry_Jynx (gCryTable[511]) with CRY_MODE_GROWL_1 (reverse, length 15, release 125, pitch 15200 = TIE key 59 + TUNE 112; the mode sets no chorus): the longest sample played backwards from its end and cut by the EOT at tick 15 (frame 18) with a release tail on a reversed DPCM channel, envelope 124, 60, 29, 14, 6, 2 on frames 18..23 and the channel stopped on frame 24

name: cry_pidgey_echo_start
note: cry_reverse Cry_Pidgey (gCryTable[403]) with CRY_MODE_ECHO_START (reverse, length 25, release 100, pitch 15600 = TIE key 61 + TUNE 56, volume 90; kept as the one-track form with chorus 0 -- cry_pidgey_echo_start_chorus is the complete mode with its chorus 192, slice 6): the 0.17 s sample is gone by frame 14, so the EOT on frame 28 finds an empty chain and the xRELE byte reaches no channel

name: cry_bulbasaur_encounter
note: Cry_Bulbasaur (gCryTable[0]) with CRY_MODE_ENCOUNTER (release 225, pitch 15600 = TIE key 61 + TUNE 56, chorus 20, volume 90; length the default 140): the first two-track cry song (SetPokemonCryChorus: trackCount 2, the second track's TUNE = (20 + 56) & 0x7F = 76), both tracks keyed on the same 8183-sample DPCM data a TUNE step apart (about 11.0 and 11.1 kHz); as in cry_bulbasaur the samples run out through the count path (around frame 50) long before the 140-tick EOT, which then finds empty chains and the mode's release 225 reaches no channel

name: cry_jynx_echo_end
note: Cry_Jynx (gCryTable[123]) with CRY_MODE_ECHO_END (release 220, pitch 15555 = TIE key 61 + TUNE 33, chorus 192, volume 70; length the default 140): the large chorus wraps the second track's TUNE to (192 + 33) & 0x7F = 97; the longest sample is still sounding on both tracks at the 140-tick EOT, so both channels are released together over the 220 tail

name: cry_pidgey_echo_start_chorus
note: cry_reverse Cry_Pidgey (gCryTable[403]) with CRY_MODE_ECHO_START complete (reverse, length 25, release 100, pitch 15600 = TIE key 61 + TUNE 56, chorus 192, volume 90): cry_pidgey_echo_start with its chorus restored, two reversed tracks with the second's TUNE (192 + 56) & 0x7F = 120; both 0.17 s samples are gone long before the EOT on frame 28
